This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a road traffic accident.

2. According to the petition averments, the deceased who was proceeding as a rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA53EM5497 succumbed to the fatal injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 03.06.2017 at about 8.30 p.m near Narayanagowda's land situated on Hosakote - Chintamani road, Nandagudi Hobli, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru District.
The said accident was caused due to the composite actionable negligence of the drivers of Mini Bus bearing Reg.KA03A7556 and Fortuner car bearing Reg.No.AP03VG3897.
Hence the respondents are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. The respondent No.1 filed written statement alleging that on 02.05.2016 he had sold the Mini Bus bearing Reg.KA03A7556 to one G. Kowstuba s/o Gopala Rao for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/.
In fact on the same day he had also handed over its possession to the said person along with the vehicular documents.
Therefore he does not have any knowledge about the alleged accident.
Contending that he is neither a necessary nor a proper party to the proceedings, payed for dismissal of the petition as against him.
4. The respondent No.2 also appeared and filed his separate written statement alleging that he was not working as a driver in respect of Mini Bus bearing Reg.KA03A7556 at any point of time.
Contending that he has been falsely implicated by the petitioners, prayed for dismissal of the petition as against him.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. The respondent No.3 filed written statement contending that at the spot of the accident the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA53EM5497 did not come into contact of Fortuner car bearing Reg.No.AP03VG3897.
Under such circumstances she is no way liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
Stating so, prayed to dismiss the petition against her.
6. The respondent No.4 filed written statement admitting the issuance of policy in respect of Fortuner car bearing Reg.No.AP03VG3897.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the driver of the mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA03A7556 was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

As such after thorough investigation the jurisdictional police have filed chargesheet against the driver and owners of mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA03A7556 for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337,
338, 304(A) of IPC and 196, 146, 3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act.
Despite being well aware of this fact the petitioners have falsely arrayed the SBI General Insurance Company as a party to the petition in order to obtain wrongful gain.

Hence prayed for dismissal of the petition against the respondent No.4.
7.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 03.06.2017 at about 8.30 p.m,
near Narayanagowda's land situated on Hosakote - Chintamani road, Nandagudi Hobli, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru District due to the composite actionable negligence of the drivers of Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA03A7556 and Fortuner car bearing Reg.No.AP03VG3897 ?
2 . Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3 . What order or award ?
8. The Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 16 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
Sri. Nagabhushan.
G s/o Late Govindappa working as an HR Manager at Medreich Limited Company, Hosakote Taluk was examined as PW.2.
Ex's .P17 to 19 were marked through this witness.
An eyewitness to the accident in question  Sri. K.M. Manjunath S/o Muninarasappa was examined as PW.3.
Initially the respondent No.1 got examined its Senior Executive as RW.1.
Ex's .R1 and 2 were marked through him.

However considering the prayer made in the memo filed by the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4 on 04.11.2022, evidence of RW.1 was discarded and the insurance company was permitted to examine other company official to prove its defence.
Accordingly on 15.11.2022, the Legal Officer of the respondent No.4 was examined as RW.2.

entities.text: Sri. Y. Ramanareddy vs ) The Head Master
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Arguments were addressed on both sides.
10. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :
Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1 : The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of the complaint lodged by one Sri. Srinivasagowda (one of the inmates of the mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA03A7556), the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed chargesheet against the driver and owners of mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA03A7556 for the offences punishable under section's 279,
337, 338, 304(A) of IPC and 196, 146, 3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Though the respondent No.2  driver of mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA03A7556 has denied the cause of the accident, he has not let in any cogent evidence to prove his defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Moreover he has not challenged the chargesheet that is filed by the jurisdictional police against him.
Thus the unchallenged chargesheet clearly establishes negligence on the part of respondent No.2.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

12. No doubt Sri. K.M. Manjunath S/o Muninarasappa (PW.3) who is alleged to have witnessed the accident in question filed affidavit evidence stating the said accident occurred due to composite actionable negligence of the drivers of Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA03A7556 and Fortuner car bearing Reg.No.AP03VG3897.
But the evidence of this witness is vague and the answers given by him during the course of crossexamination raises serious doubt about his presence at the spot of the accident.

Further though he stated that the police have recorded his statement and that he has affixed his signature on the spot mahazar as a witness, neither the copy of his statement is produced before the Court nor is his signature found in Ex.P4Spot Mahazar.
He is also not cited as an eyewitness or mahazar witness in the chargesheet.
Admittedly the mini bus was not insured at the time of accident.

Hence it appears that PW.3 who resides very close to the house of the petitioners might on their request would have deposed falsely on their behalf in order to enable them to claim compensation from the insurer of Fortuner car bearing Reg.No.AP03VG3897.

Be that as it may,
holding that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA03A 7556, issue No.1 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
13. ISSUE NO.2 :
The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chiefexamination and deposed that he is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioners No.3 to 5 are the elder sisters of the deceased.
The documents placed on record reflect the aforesaid relationship of the claimants with the deceased.
Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased 'Sri. P. Sivasankara Reddy'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well settled that dependency must be established in order to claim compensation.
However during the course of his crossexamination PW.1 admitted that the petitioners No.3 to 5 are married and are residing at their husband's house.
In this view of matter petitioners No.3 to 5 cannot be said to be dependents on the earnings of their deceased brother.
Under such circumstances only the petitioners No.1 & 2 are entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of dependency'.
15. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS : In the Aadhar card (Ex.P11) the year of birth of deceased is reflected as 1991.
This indicates that he was aged 26 years on the date of accident.

The appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '17'.
16.
In order to substantiate the fact the deceased was working as a Quality Assurance Officer at Medreich, Bengaluru, the petitioners got examined the employer of the deceased as PW.2.
This witness deposed that the deceased was working in their company since 26.12.2016.
PW.2 has produced the appointment letter, salary slips and wage register statements of the deceased, which are exhibited at Ex's.P17 to 19.
The testimony of this witness which is fortified by the said exhibits was not displaced during crossexamination.
As per Ex.P.18 the annual gross salary of the deceased was Rs.2,27,457/.
The said annual income is below taxable limit.
However professional tax needs to be deducted from it.

The calculation table for which stands as follows :
 Gross Income 2,27,457  Less Annual Professional Tax 2400  Annual Established Income 2,25,057

Monthly Established Income 18,755  (2,25,057 / 12)
17.
There is nothing on record to show that the deceased was a permanent employee.
In the case on hand the deceased was aged 26 years.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SCC 5157,
40% of income is to be added towards future prospects.

40% of Rs.18,755/ works out to Rs.7,502/
.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.26,257/ (18,755 + 7,502).

The deceased was bachelor and as such in view of the proposition of Law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma's case, half of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.

1/2 of Rs.26,257/
works out to Rs.13,128/.
Income for consideration is Rs.13,129/ ( 26,257 - 13,128).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,57,548/ (13,129 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '17'.

Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.26,78,316 (1,57,548 X 17) which is rounded off to Rs.26,79,000/.
18.
LOSS OF CONSORTIUM :
In addition to a sum of Rs.26,79,000/ towards Loss of dependency the petitioners No.1 & 2 are also entitled to Rs.40,000/ each towards filial consortium.

) Sri. Y. Ramanareddy vs ) The Head Master on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196052730/
5 19.

entities.text: Sri. Y. Ramanareddy vs ) The Head Master
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: LOSS OF ESTATE:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards loss of estate.
20. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards funeral expenses.

21. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : 26,79,00000 2 Loss of Consortium : 80,00000 3 Loss of Estate : 15,00000 4
Funeral Expenses : 15,00000 Total 27,89,00000 22.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
In the light of detailed discussion made in Issue No.1, this Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the driver of Mini Bus bearing Reg.KA 03A7556 was negligent in causing the accident.

As such the petition deserves to be dismissed against the respondents No.3 and 4 i.e, owner and insurer of the Fortuner car bearing Reg.No.AP03VG3897.
23.

The specific contention of the respondent No.1 is that on 02.05.2016 he had sold the Mini Bus bearing Reg.KA03A7556 to one G. Kowstuba s/o Gopala Rao for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ and on the same day he had handed over the possession thereof to him along with vehicular documents.
But as evident from the police records as on the date of accident, the RC of the Mini Bus bearing Reg.KA03A7556 still stood in the name of respondent No.1.
As per Sec.2(30) of the MV Act it is the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands registered, would be treated as owner of the vehicle for the purposes of the said act.

In the case of Naveen Kumar V/s Vijay Kumar and others reported in (2018) 3 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that 'In view of the definition of the expression 'owner' in Section 2(30) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, it is the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands registered, who, for the purposes of the said act, would be treated as owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: Naveen Kumar V/s Vijay Kumar and others reported in (2018) 3 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where the registered owner purports to transfer the vehicle but continues to be reflected in the records of the Registering Authority as the owner of the vehicle, he would not stand absolved of his liability as owner'.
(Emphasis supplied)

Relying upon the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the decision cited supra, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'
24.
ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby dismissed against respondent No.2 to 4 and allowed in part as against respondent No.1 with costs in the following terms :

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.27,89,000/ (Rupees Twenty Seven Lakhs Eighty Nine Thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1  Rs.13,79,500/

 Petitioner No.3  Rs.10,000/

Out of the share amount of Petitioners No.1 & 2

a sum equal to 25% each shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioners No.3 to 5 through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw an award accordingly.
